name: Wheat
fact: Wheat was one of the first crops ever domesticated, in the Fertile Crescent about 11,000 years ago.

name: Barley
fact: Barley was used for bread, porridge and beer in many ancient societies.

name: Oats
fact: Oats grow well in cool, wet climates like northern Europe.

name: Rye
fact: Rye tolerates cold and poor soils, so it was important in northern and eastern Europe.

name: Millet
fact: Millets are hardy grains, farmed in northern China and across Africa's Sahel for thousands of years.

name: Sorghum
fact: Sorghum was domesticated in Africa and thrives in hot, dry conditions.

name: Teff
fact: Teff, a tiny grain from the Ethiopian Highlands, is used to make injera flatbread.

name: Rice
fact: Rice was domesticated in the Yangtze valley in China. It is grown in flooded paddies that keep weeds down.

name: Maize
fact: Maize (corn) was bred from teosinte in southern Mexico about 9,000 years ago.

name: Beans
fact: Beans add nitrogen to the soil, which helps neighbouring maize grow.

name: Squash
fact: Squash was among the first plants domesticated in the Americas, over 8,000 years ago.

name: Potatoes
fact: Andean farmers developed thousands of potato varieties suited to different altitudes.

name: Quinoa
fact: Quinoa has been grown in the Andes for thousands of years and tolerates cold, high places.

name: Cassava
fact: Cassava, from South America, has starchy roots and grows well in poor tropical soils.

name: Yams
fact: Yams are a staple food in West Africa, where yam festivals celebrate the harvest.

name: Taro
fact: Taro was carried across the Pacific by Polynesian voyagers.

name: Sweet potato
fact: The sweet potato, from the Americas, reached Polynesia before European voyages. How it got there is still studied.

name: Breadfruit
fact: Breadfruit trees were planted widely on Pacific islands for their starchy fruit.

name: Soybeans
fact: Soybeans were domesticated in northern China and are used for tofu, soy sauce and oil.

name: Tea
fact: Tea drinking spread widely in China during the Tang dynasty.

name: Cotton
fact: Cotton was domesticated separately in South Asia, Africa and the Americas.

name: Sugarcane
fact: Sugarcane was first domesticated in New Guinea and spread to South Asia, where sugar crystals were first made.

name: Sugar beet
fact: Sugar beet became a major source of sugar in Europe during the 1800s.

name: Flax
fact: Flax fibres are spun into linen, the main cloth of ancient Egypt.

name: Lentils
fact: Lentils were among the founder crops of Neolithic farming.

name: Olive grove
fact: Olive trees can live for hundreds or even thousands of years.

name: Vineyard
fact: Grapevines are trained along rows of posts so they get plenty of sun.

name: Date grove
fact: Date palms were cultivated in Mesopotamia and Egypt for thousands of years.

name: Coconut grove
fact: Coconuts provide food, drink, oil, rope fibre and building materials.

name: Banana garden
fact: Bananas were domesticated in New Guinea and Southeast Asia thousands of years ago.

name: Cacao grove
fact: Mesoamericans made cacao into a frothy drink long before chocolate bars existed.

name: Coffee
fact: Coffee plants are native to Ethiopia. Coffee drinking spread from Yemen in the 1400s.

name: Chili peppers
fact: Chili peppers come from the Americas and spread around the world after 1500.
